references.text: The priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven. This verse describes the priest's role in making atonement through a sin offering.
The sin offering and guilt offering that the priest presents to make atonement for the one who has sinned.
The burnt offering that makes atonement for the one who brings it forward.
The priest shall offer the sin offering and make atonement for the one who is to be cleansed from their uncleanness.
Atonement for a sin committed against a person (נֶפֶשׁ), using the same expression found in Num 6:11.
The Nazirite shall bring his offerings to the Lord, including a sin offering and a burnt offering, as part of the Nazirite vow.
The Levites shall lay their hands on the bulls, one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering, to make atonement.
The consecration of the head (נֵזֶר) in connection with priestly service and dedication.
The book of Hebrews explains how Christ's blood cleanses the conscience from dead works, unlike Old Testament sacrifices which only provided external purity.
The law with its offerings could never make those who drew near perfect; animal blood cannot take away sins. This points forward to the perfect sacrifice in Christ.
